findings.body:
**Restore the seeded queue even if process cleanup fails.**

If `stop_process()` raises during cleanup, this `finally` exits before restoring the saved queue or removing the seeded run metadata. A later switch or recovery then starts with test work still in the queue. The harvest and recovery-drain phases use the same cleanup ordering.

Register each cleanup action independently, so a process cleanup error remains visible but cannot skip queue restoration or run-metadata cleanup.
findings.title: Restore the seeded queue even if process cleanup fails.

findings.body:
**Bind the reboot check to the final inspection.**

If the before and after snapshots both report boot ID A, but the reboot poll reports B, `boot_id_changed` still passes. The report can then verify even though the snapshot that supplies the mask evidence does not prove a new boot.

Require the poll IDs to match their respective snapshot IDs. Then require distinct, nonempty before and after IDs.
findings.title: Bind the reboot check to the final inspection.

findings.body:
**Use the remaining readiness budget for cloud-init.**

If SSH first responds near the end of the 240-second readiness window, `cloud-init status --wait` gets another 240 seconds. The command can take nearly twice the stated timeout before it reports failure. Use a monotonic deadline and cap each SSH call and sleep to the remaining budget.
findings.title: Use the remaining readiness budget for cloud-init.

findings.body:
**Bind the executed scripts to `source_commit`.**

A run can supply HEAD as `--source-commit` while executing a modified guest script from the working tree. Upload and artifact verification still pass because both compare against the modified bytes. Neither check establishes that HEAD contains those bytes.

Run the scripts from the stated commit, or verify the exact script bytes against trusted blobs from that commit before recording provenance.
findings.title: Bind the executed scripts to `sourcecommit`.

findings.body:
**Do not share a writable image staging file across invocations.**

Two fetches against an empty state directory can open the same `.part` file. One can verify and promote that file while the other still has it open for writing. If Ubuntu changes the image between requests, the second writer can change the promoted base after verification, including while a run opens an overlay backed by it.

Lock cache population and recheck the cache under that lock. Use private staging files and do not replace an installed base that existing overlays reference.
findings.title: Do not share a writable image staging file across invocations.

findings.body:
**Check for completions before the pause callback starts.**

A queued Python start can complete after `completions_before` is read at Line 2291 but before `during()` takes its first sample. Both callback samples then include that completion. `external_completion_delta` is zero, and the two later Node completions can still satisfy every invocation check.

Compare the first pause sample with the pre-switch log as well as comparing the two callback samples. This detects work that completed before the external activation tests began.
findings.title: Check for completions before the pause callback starts.

findings.body:
**Validate phase-specific arguments before dispatch.**

On `crq-probe`, `matrix-restart-drained-observe` without `--boundary` reaches `MATRIX_CASES[None]` and returns a runtime `KeyError`. A different valid `--boundary` can instead select the wrong retained case. Derive the matrix case from the phase name. Reject missing inputs such as `--record` on recovery phases as usage errors before dispatch.

As per coding guidelines, doctrine I1 assigns “1 thrown error, 2 arg error.” Python 3.11's parser error path supports the usage exit; use the repository's JSON error format on that path. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/argparse.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Validate phase-specific arguments before dispatch.

findings.body:
**Reject a second boot while the run already owns a live VM.**

After a successful `boot`, repeating `boot --run-id` leaves the original `qemu.pid` in place. The second launch reads that PID without proving it belongs to the new launch. It can then pass SSH readiness against the old VM. If readiness or upload fails, the second invocation can instead stop the old VM during cleanup.

Serialize lifecycle changes for the run. Reject a live run before launching or entering cleanup, and capture fresh process identity for a stopped run.
findings.title: Reject a second boot while the run already owns a live VM.

findings.body:
**Keep runtime integrity failures distinct from usage errors.**

If `fetch` finds a corrupted cached image, `verify_image` raises `ValueError`. This handler returns exit 2 even though the arguments are valid. Use a dedicated usage or refusal exception. Keep a missing `--source-commit` at exit 2 and report an image integrity failure at exit 1.

As per coding guidelines, doctrine I1 assigns “1 thrown error, 2 arg error.”
findings.title: Keep runtime integrity failures distinct from usage errors.

findings.body:
**Require the target start job to be waiting before cancellation.**

This control accepts any target `start` job with no completion logged yet. If the blocker exits before the sample, the job can be running. Stopping it and observing no completion does not prove cancellation of a waiting job. Match the exact target unit, `start` type, and `waiting` state. Apply the same check to the fence seed at Line 2283.
findings.title: Require the target start job to be waiting before cancellation.

findings.body:
**Hold the fence pause until the observation callback returns.**

`_maybe_pause` ends after a fixed wall-clock interval, not after the harness finishes its observations. The adapter writes the marker, sleeps for up to `pause_seconds` (default 20 s, capped at 30 s), and then continues the switch. `cli_paused` runs `during()` synchronously after it sees the marker, and nothing signals the adapter when that callback completes. The callback can therefore run past the pause. When it does, its later samples can reflect adapter-driven state, such as the service stop and drain that follow the pause, rather than the paused fence. The proof must not attribute those samples to the paused window.

Require that the pause end only after the callback reports completion, or that the proof abort when the callback does not complete within its bound. A timeout alone must not allow the switch to continue while the callback is still collecting evidence.
findings.title: Hold the fence pause until the observation callback returns.
